vulnerability_mechanism.evidence: Claimed CWE-639 path (authenticated client revokes another client's key by supplying a valid ML-DSA signature) was traced on both implementations at parent 4b2adb05cde8a7ee03cdd271755da3b377c68011. Unified openssl_encrypt_server/modules/keyserver/service.py:195-270 (the vendor-cited sink) looks up KSKey by fingerprint, loads that record's bundle_json signing_public_key, and only then calls verify_revocation_signature; client_id is passed only to _log_access and is never compared to owner_client_id (models.py:56 comments owner_client_id as 'Optional: track uploader'). Standalone server/key-server/app/api/v1/keys.py:324-380 does the same cryptographic gate (any valid Bearer token plus target-bundle public key). verification.py:187-245 (standalone; unified copy is equivalent) runs oqs.Signature.verify(fingerprint.encode('utf-8'), supplied_signature, target_public_key) and raises VerificationError on failure, so the revoked=True mutation is not reached without the target private key. A signature that merely verifies under some other client's key cannot authorize revocation of the selected fingerprint. Official CVE record https://cveawg.mitre.org/api/cve/CVE-2026-74877 remains cveMetadata.state=PUBLISHED (not rejected/withdrawn); GitHub GHSA-hmf7-54mh-cvp4 withdrawn_at is null and is unreviewed. Vendor GHSA-hvc7-763r-4f3h itself states the signature requires the private key and that the 'fix' documents ML-DSA verification as the cryptographic ownership check. The claimed unauthorized source-to-sink therefore does not exist.

atomic_bic.evidence: No bug-introducing commit exists because the claimed missing-ownership mechanism is absent from first public write. fafdfeed1b279cfe61e86cd8adc132b206eef8d4 (single parent 4c7ae852c784c9986d087c5956a77fa563a05a35; parent tree has no server/key-server/) already implemented revoke_key with verify_revocation_signature against the target bundle's signing_public_key and docstring 'proof of ownership'. 8170b3e0be064cdaddbc8ef51c17e21c42d2d3f4 copied the same gate into openssl_encrypt_server/modules/keyserver/service.py:195-270. Search was not inverted onto AI-marked commits; those first-writes were inspected only as the earliest public objects containing the revoke path.

immediate_parent_absence.evidence: No BIC, so no parent-absence claim for a vulnerability. For completeness: 4c7ae852c784c9986d087c5956a77fa563a05a35 (parent of fafdfeed1b279cfe61e86cd8adc132b206eef8d4) has no key-server tree (git ls-tree shows only keyserver_plan.md). The cryptographic revocation gate appears as a first-write of a new surface, already requiring target-key proof, not as a later omission of an ownership check that the parent had.

squash_member_decomposition.evidence: Alleged fix 05e45f393886b5bf7e924d2dd42099a9dd37f91d is a single-parent commit (parent 4b2adb05cde8a7ee03cdd271755da3b377c68011), not a merge or squash aggregate; git diff-tree --name-status reports only M server/key-server/app/api/v1/keys.py (+8/-1 comments and an info log). fafdfeed1b279cfe61e86cd8adc132b206eef8d4 and 8170b3e0be064cdaddbc8ef51c17e21c42d2d3f4 are large first-write features with one parent each; neither conceals a reconstructable member that added an unauthorized revoke sink. No member SHA needs to replace either object.

affected_release_membership.evidence: CVE/VulnCheck label versions < 1.4.0 affected. v1.3.6 is f69305effbab0bdc0c8df0f2297cdfddf8929b6e and does not contain the keyserver (git merge-base --is-ancestor fafdfeed1b279cfe61e86cd8adc132b206eef8d4 v1.3.6 exits 1). First tag containing the revoke path is v1.4.0 (768df5cd1910e349509f07a27eeac6951e0003bf). On every tree that actually implements revoke_key, including 4b2adb05cde8a7ee03cdd271755da3b377c68011 and 8170b3e0be064cdaddbc8ef51c17e21c42d2d3f4, the target-key signature gate is already present, so there is no genuinely affected release membership for the claimed bypass.

fixed_release_membership.evidence: git rev-parse v1.4.0^{commit} = 768df5cd1910e349509f07a27eeac6951e0003bf. git merge-base --is-ancestor 05e45f393886b5bf7e924d2dd42099a9dd37f91d v1.4.0 exits 0, so the vendor-pointed object is in the claimed fixed tag. git diff 8170b3e0be064cdaddbc8ef51c17e21c42d2d3f4 v1.4.0 -- openssl_encrypt_server/modules/keyserver/service.py openssl_encrypt_server/modules/keyserver/verification.py is empty: the vendor-cited unified revoke_key is byte-identical in the 'patched' release. v1.4.0 therefore ships documentation/logging on the standalone route and no authorization-predicate change on either route.

direct_fix_or_unpatched.evidence: Direct 'fix' 05e45f393886b5bf7e924d2dd42099a9dd37f91d (author/committer Tobi <tobster@brain-force.ch>) changes only comments and logger.info in server/key-server/app/api/v1/keys.py; git show --numstat is 8/1 on that single file. The message states revocation signature verification IS the ownership check and is stronger than account-based checks. No client_id == owner_client_id predicate, 403 branch, or other authorization change is introduced. Unified service.py is untouched. That is not a security fix of a missing check; it is vendor disposition that the existing cryptographic gate was the intended control.

bic_only_ai_attribution.evidence: No real vulnerability and therefore no BIC on which to read author/committer/Co-Authored-By/Generated-with markers. AI trailers on fafdfeed1b279cfe61e86cd8adc132b206eef8d4, 8170b3e0be064cdaddbc8ef51c17e21c42d2d3f4, and 05e45f393886b5bf7e924d2dd42099a9dd37f91d were not used to select an introducer. Attribution is inapplicable for FALSE_POSITIVE.

CVE-2026-74877 remains PUBLISHED at https://cveawg.mitre.org/api/cve/CVE-2026-74877 (CNA VulnCheck; dateUpdated 2026-08-18T14:36:53.489Z). GitHub GHSA-hmf7-54mh-cvp4 is unreviewed with withdrawn_at null. GitHub withdrawn_at is not treated as authoritative.

Vendor GHSA-hvc7-763r-4f3h names openssl_encrypt_server/modules/keyserver/service.py lines 195-270, admits a valid revocation signature requires the private key, calls the missing client_id check a defense-in-depth gap, and records the fix as documentation that ML-DSA verification IS the cryptographic ownership check (commit 05e45f393886b5bf7e924d2dd42099a9dd37f91d).

At 4b2adb05cde8a7ee03cdd271755da3b377c68011 both revoke implementations bind authorization to the target record's signing_public_key. An authenticated attacker who does not hold that private key cannot complete the sink. Possession of a valid target-key signature is cryptographic ownership, not a bypass of an intended account restriction.
owner_client_id is stored as optional uploader telemetry (nullable column) and is never read as an authorization identity. client_id on the unified path is used only for KSAccessLog.

05e45f393886b5bf7e924d2dd42099a9dd37f91d is comments plus an info log on the standalone keys.py route. Unified service.py/verification.py are identical between 8170b3e0be064cdaddbc8ef51c17e21c42d2d3f4 and v1.4.0 768df5cd1910e349509f07a27eeac6951e0003bf.

The revoke surface does not exist in v1.3.6; it first appears as a first-write that already required target-key proof. There is no BIC, no affected-release membership for the claimed bypass, and no behavioral security fix.

Primary FALSE_POSITIVE is independently supported. Not NOT_AI: there is no real vulnerability whose human authorship would be scored. Not CORRECTION_REQUIRED: the claimed impact is disproved, not merely mis-versioned.
